 Taxation & Economic Development Application Deadline for Property Tax Relief Programs is Nov. 2
 Published 
 October 23
 SHARE
 Twitter
 Facebook
 LinkedIn
 The New Jersey Treasury’s Division of Taxation is urging eligible residents to apply for the State’s property tax relief programs by the Nov. 2 deadline.
 Seniors aged 65 and older and disabled homeowners or mobile homeowners can apply for the ANCHOR, Senior Freeze, and Stay NJ property tax relief programs through the PAS-1 application.
 The PAS-1 replaced the former Senior Freeze and ANCHOR applications, so eligible taxpayers no longer need to file separate applications for these programs. The application also applies to New Jersey’s newest property tax relief program, Stay NJ.
 Residents should file the 2025 PAS-1 application if their income for Tax Year 2025 was under $500,000. The Division of Taxation will determine which programs taxpayers are eligible for and calculate the benefits they are entitled to receive.
 “The PAS-1 application allows seniors and disabled residents to apply for all of New Jersey’s property tax relief programs at one time and makes the process as seamless as possible,” said State Treasurer Aaron Binder.
 Residents under the age of 65 who own or rent property in New Jersey can also benefit from property tax relief through the ANCHOR program by applying via the ANC-1 application.
 Both the PAS-1 and ANC-1 forms can be found and submitted online at propertytaxreliefapp.nj.gov , where residents can also check the status of their benefit, view frequently asked questions and access detailed information on each program. The deadline to file both applications is Nov. 2, 2026.
